newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 22.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - April 22.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Tuesday and main factors likely to affect trading.
* Philippine stocks are likely to open weak on Tuesday due to lack of new incentives, traders said.

* The cancellation of trading on Monday at the Philippine Stock Exchange may keep some investors at the sidelines, they said. "A lot of investors were really disappointed. Some (foreign investors) may begin to think this was intentional," said Henry Ong, research head at Sapphire Securities.
* Traders said the softness of Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co's ADRs in New York in the past two trading sessions will add to the selling pressure in the market.
* The main index is seen finding its floor at the 2,880 level. It closed on Friday at 2,944.48 points, up 17.11.
* The peso closed on Monday at 26.361 to a dollar
* Interbank call loan average was unchanged at 10.03125 percent.

* Lepanto Consolidated Mining Co expects brighter prospects in the next two years, with net income seen rising to one billion pesos in 1998 after its discovery of a new gold mine in northern Philippines, officials said on Monday.
The Victoria project in Benguet province is expected to push up Lepanto's net income to at least 648 million pesos this year compared with 45.7 million pesos in 1996.
* Oil refiner Petron Corp is set to redefine its corporate structure and public image in the face of growing competition in a newly deregulated industry, Petron officials said on Monday.
The programme will cost at least 200 million pesos ($7.6 million).
* Petron Corp said on Monday it expects to increase its sales volume by more than the industry average.
"We are targetting to outpace the industry's growth of over six percent annually," Petron president Ali Al-Ajmi told reporters after the stockholders' meeting.
Last year overall sales rose eight percent to a record high of 58.73 million barrels from 54.27 million the previous year.
* A top official of gold miner Manila Mining Co said on Monday the company was considering a merger with Lepanto Consolidated Mining Co.

* Manila Mining Corp posted a net loss of 38 million pesos in the first quarter of the year due to lower grades of gold mined, president Artemio Disini said on Monday during the stockholders' meeting.
